previous_statement: Apply coordinate extraction. Let Z=Gamma_n mu_n(X)=(gamma_jk,n(X_jk)) and gamma_n(X)=alpha_n(Z). The datum two-sided norm clause and node 1.1.1 give ||Z||_max>=(1-rho)max||X_jk||>=(1-rho)||X||/4 and ||gamma_n(X)||<=sum(1+rho)||X_jk||<=4(1+rho)||X||. Node 1.1.2 gives (1-3L_c e)||Z||_max<=||beta alpha Z||_max<=M_c||gamma_n(X)||. Taking e_blk<=min{1/4,(6L_c)^(-1)} yields ||gamma_n(X)||>=||X||/(8M_c) and ||gamma_n(X)||<=5||X||. Thus c_blk=1/(8M_c), B_blk=5 work universally.
new_statement: Apply coordinate extraction. Let Z=Gamma_n mu_n(X)=(gamma_jk,n(X_jk)) and gamma_n(X)=alpha_n(Z). The datum two-sided norm clause and node 1.1.1 give ||Z||_max>=(1-rho)max||X_jk||>=(1-rho)||X||/4 and ||gamma_n(X)||<=sum_jk (1+rho)||X_jk||<=4(1+rho)||X||. Node 1.1.2 gives (1-3L_c e)||Z||_max<=||beta alpha Z||_max<=M_c||gamma_n(X)||. Therefore ||gamma_n(X)||>=((1-3L_c e)(1-rho)/(4M_c))||X||. Take e_blk=min{1/8,(12L_c)^(-1)}. Since rho<=e<=e_blk, one has 1-3L_c e>=3/4 and 1-rho>=7/8, hence ||gamma_n(X)||>=21||X||/(128M_c)>=||X||/(16M_c); also ||gamma_n(X)||<=4(1+rho)||X||<=5||X||. Thus c_blk=1/(16M_c), B_blk=5 work universally.
